themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it. So the models start by building a small set of cases they can actually prove, then grade everything else against that.
themes.evidence: Answer engine work starts with a fixed panel of real buyer questions because answers shift run to run; identity resolution starts with a logged-in panel because nobody knows who is really the same person; incrementality starts with always-on holdouts because platforms re-optimize against the test; and today's semantic context answers begin by counting how many conflicting definitions are already running in production.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls are about meaning and worth, not data: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, what the word customer means. No formula settles these, because the disagreement usually has budget attached.
themes.evidence: Today all three models say conflicting definitions of customer and revenue are a political fight between teams defending their own numbers, not a modeling gap; the same shape appears in content review, where reviewers catch implied claims that no single approved element asserts, and in journey orchestration, where nobody can price a sale today against fatigue tomorrow.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be called back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Agent execution answers converge on a proxy or gateway with hard spend and audience caps; consent enforcement answers route every data exit through a single checkpoint; journey orchestration answers build one shared send log with veto power; and today's semantic layer answers strip tool access and route agents through pre-aggregated, warehouse-defined endpoints.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a dollar, or a message leaves your own systems, you cannot look inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. The best anyone offers is watching from the outside and hoping the behavior matches the promise.
themes.evidence: Consent answers agree that deletion inside walled gardens and trained models cannot be proven, only sampled with canary profiles and expiring lists; agent execution answers note vendors expose no rollback or agent identity; and today's semantic layer answers warn that permissions cannot follow an agent into platforms that have no notion of them.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by handing it over, and nobody can force them. So the models either try to make honesty pay better than hiding, or they stop waiting for cooperation and work only with what they already own.
themes.evidence: Agent traffic answers build a fast declared-agent lane because agents gain by looking human; identity answers note platform owners profit from broken cross-device links; ad supply answers say the parties measuring fraud profit from the traffic; and today's semantic answers say teams actively resist aligning definitions that defend their budgets.
